sentences.text: This extinct neosuchian crocodyliform resided in the Wessex Formation of England.
It belongs to the family Bernissartiidae.
An isolated tooth found by Megan Jacobs was twice the size of the holotype teeth.
Initial identification suggested the small, button-shaped teeth belonged to Bernissartia fagesii.
Diane Trevarthen found the first skull fragment on a beach near Sandown in March 2011.
Austin and Finley Nathan located a second fragment just three months later.
Steve Sweetman and colleagues formally named the species in a 2015 paper.
The animal lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
The family Bernissartiidae is recovered as the sister group to Eusuchia.
